title: Part Five: Free Speech for Whom

sections.brief: State action doctrine: Halleck 2019 (5-4); Citizens United (5-4 on the spending ban, 8-1 upholding disclosure); Moody v. NetChoice 2024 (9-0 vacate; editorial choices); corporations hold speech rights in both directions, users none against them; Meta super PAC and inaugural gifts; Pew 2024/2026 knowledge and opinion; two readings. Figures: compare (three parties); flow (sorting a complaint)

Moderation in every direction on one standard: HRW 2023 (self-reported caveat) and Meta's reply; BSR 2022 disparate impact, causes not intent; Oversight Board on shaheed and 'river to the sea'; Meta's 'Zionist'-as-proxy rule; Musk's opposite stance; TikTok JV 2026; laptop story (Dorsey, Zuckerberg), Twitter Files, Trump suspension and restoration, Meta Jan 2025. Figures: compare (cases with company positions); time (2020-2026)

Where users have rights: Vullo 2024 (9-0) and Murthy 2024 (standing); Biden-era (Zuckerberg letter, White House reply, EO 14149) and Trump-era (Carr/Kimmel, Paramount conditions) on one footing; routes to undo Citizens United: Article V, Democracy for All 54-42 (2014) reintroduced 2025, reversal, Montana I-194 on the 3 Nov 2026 ballot; the test. Figures: compare (two administrations); flow (routes)
